title: Count Number of Pairs With Absolute Difference K
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, count the number of pairs (i, j) where i < j and the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] equals k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, count the number of pairs (i, j) where i < j and the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] equals k. The absolute value |x| is the value of x if x is non-negative, and -x if x is negative.
constraints: nums has 1 through 200 integers and k is nonnegative.
Count index pairs i<j with absolute difference exactly k.
Duplicate values at different indices form distinct pairs.
hints: When the later value arrives, count all earlier values exactly k away.
Maintain frequencies and query value-k and value+k, taking care not to query zero distance twice.
Add count[x-k], plus count[x+k] when k>0; then record x.
Every i<j pair is considered once at j, and the two queried values are exactly the solutions to |nums[i]-nums[j]|=k.
editorial: Every i<j pair is considered once at j, and the two queried values are exactly the solutions to |nums[i]-nums[j]|=k.

tests.explanation: Each one pairs with each two, producing four index pairs.
Their difference is two, so no pair qualifies.
